title: Chicken 65
description: Spicy yoghurt-marinated chicken, crisped in the air fryer. Four portions to have with dal, add to fried rice or serve as an extra side with a curry.
portionNote: The full batch uses 1 kg chicken breast and makes 4 portions. Serve with dal for a complete meal, add it to fried rice or have it as an extra side with a curry.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of red, spice-coated Chicken 65 pieces with a green herb garnish on a simple white plate.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · fried Chicken 65 with a herb garnish · displayed crop
personalNote: Mix the marinade straight in a Tupperware so we don’t have another bowl to wash. Give it at least an hour in the fridge, but a few hours or overnight is much better if we’ve got time.
equipment: Tupperware with a lid, large enough for the chicken
advancePrep: Defrost the 4 ginger-garlic cubes so they become a paste. Plan for at least 1 hour of fridge time after coating the chicken; a few hours or overnight is better.
importantNotes: Taste and adjust the seasoned yoghurt mixture before adding flour or raw chicken. The chicken cubes should be similar sizes, so they cook evenly. Air fry in a single layer at 180°C for 30 minutes per batch, flipping and shaking halfway, then shaking again at the end. Use both baskets or extra batches if needed.

ingredients.name: Ginger-garlic cubes
ingredients.note: Defrost fully so they become a paste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Taste the marinade before the flour and raw chicken go in; adjust if needed.

ingredients.name: Plain yoghurt
ingredients.note: Keep a tiny bit extra handy if the coating is too thick.

ingredients.name: Oil spray
ingredients.note: Spray the bottom of the baskets and the tops of the chicken pieces.

steps.title: Make the seasoned yoghurt straight in the Tupperware
steps.description: Use a clean Tupperware instead of a bowl. Mix the defrosted ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, salt, yoghurt, lime juice and curry leaves together.

steps.title: Taste it before the flour or chicken goes in
steps.description: Give this mixture a taste now and adjust the salt and spices if needed. It should taste really salty and spicy — that will mellow out once it coats all the chicken. Do this taste test before adding the flours or raw chicken.

steps.title: Mix in the two flours
steps.description: Add the cornflour and rice flour or ground rice. Mix them through the marinade until it’s all combined.

steps.title: Cube the chicken and coat it properly
steps.description: Chop the chicken breast into similar-sized cubes and add it to the Tupperware. Mix it around until all the pieces are coated. If the mixture is too thick to coat them, add a tiny bit more yoghurt and mix again.
steps.tip: Similar-sized pieces will cook more evenly. Don’t taste the marinade after the raw chicken has gone in.

steps.title: Lid on and into the fridge
steps.description: Put the lid on and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour. A few hours or overnight is much better if we’ve planned ahead.
steps.tip: The one-hour timer is the minimum marination time. Leave it longer in the fridge if we’ve got time.

steps.title: Oil the baskets and leave the chicken in one layer
steps.description: Spray the bottom of the air fryer baskets with oil. Lay the chicken pieces out in a single layer, then spray the tops with oil too. Use both baskets or cook in batches if we need more space; the pieces need room to crisp.

steps.title: Air fry the first 15 minutes
steps.description: Put the chicken into the air fryer at 180°C and cook for the first 15 minutes.

steps.title: Halfway: flip and shake
steps.description: Flip the chicken pieces with tongs and give the baskets a shake so the pieces move around and crisp on the other sides.

steps.title: Another 15 minutes at 180°C
steps.description: Return the baskets to the air fryer and cook for another 15 minutes at 180°C. That makes 30 minutes of cooking altogether for this batch.

steps.title: One last shake, then check the middle
steps.description: Give the baskets another shake at the end. Check a few of the thickest chicken pieces are fully cooked through before serving. We want crisp edges and hot, cooked chicken inside. If any pieces need more time, put them back in and check again.
steps.doneness: Crisp coating and chicken that is steaming hot through the middle. A clean food thermometer in a thick piece should read at least 75°C.

steps.title: With dal, in fried rice or beside a curry
steps.description: This makes 4 portions. Serve with dal to make a complete meal, add the cooked pieces to fried rice or have them as an extra side with a curry. The dal and the cooked-chicken fried rice recipes are linked below.

substitutions.title: Rice flour or ground rice
substitutions.text: Use 1 tablespoon of either, along with the 2 tablespoons of cornflour.

substitutions.title: The coating is too thick
substitutions.text: Add a tiny bit of extra yoghurt and mix it through so the marinade coats all the chicken.

substitutions.title: Make it a meal
substitutions.text: Serve Chicken 65 with the dal for a complete meal. It also works mixed into fried rice, or as an extra side with a curry.

troubleshooting.title: The chicken isn’t crisp enough
troubleshooting.text: Leave space between the pieces, spray the tops with oil and remember the halfway flip and shake, plus another shake at the end. Use extra batches if needed instead of stacking the pieces.

troubleshooting.title: One batch won’t fit
troubleshooting.text: Use both baskets or cook in separate single-layer batches. The 30-minute cooking time is for each batch; allow more time if cooking batches one after another.

storage: Marinate in the covered Tupperware in the fridge. If preparing ahead, a few hours or overnight is better. Cool cooked leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours; use within 2 days.
reheating: Reheat only the portion we’re eating, once, until steaming hot throughout. If adding saved Chicken 65 to fried rice, heat the pieces through fully with the rice.
foodSafety: Taste the seasoned yoghurt before adding flour or raw chicken. Once the chicken is in, don’t taste the raw marinade. Check the thickest chicken pieces reach at least 75°C before serving.
servingSuggestion: Four portions. Serve with Simple Tarka Dal for a complete meal, add to fried rice or have as an extra side with a curry.
